question.problem: While hunting, a lioness accelerates from rest with a constant acceleration of $5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ for the first $4$ seconds of her motion. Then, the lioness decelerates with a constant deceleration of $4\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ until she stops. Which graph represents the described motion?
question.worked_solution:
We start the first line from the point $(0,0),$ since the lioness is starting from rest. Then, because the acceleration is $5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ we draw a line with slope $5.$ 

However, because the lioness is only accelerating for the first $4$ seconds, we stop the line at $t=4.$ At this time, the lioness' speed has increased by $5\cdot 4=20\,\text{m/s}.$ So, the first line segment goes from $(0,0)$ to $(4,20).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14265567/assets/62780dd4c7ae5f8a3b674dd8fef84e16d7483b46bea675f078f8169947dd55f3.png)

After $t=4,$ the lioness has a deceleration of $4\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ so the slope of the second line segment is $-4.$ The second line segment stops when the lioness' speed returns to $0.$ To figure out when this is, we need to find the equation for the second line segment.

Since the second line segment passes through the point $(4,20)$ and has a slope of $-4,$ we can use point-slope form to write the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}v-{v}_{1} & =m(t-{t}_{1}) \\ v-20 & =-4(t-4) \\ v-20 & =-4t+16 \\ v & =-4t+36\end{aligned}
$$

We solve for $t$ when the speed of the lioness is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =-4t+36 \\ 0 & =-4t+36 \\ 4t & =36 \\ t & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second line segment stops at the point $(9,0).$ The final graph is
